name: Safety Glass
desc: A pane failing over and over: impacts nucleate one at a time, radial cracks run outward at finite speed and arrest ragged, Hertzian rings bow in behind the tips, a crumb zone blooms at the strike and glints crawl the fractures — while the oldest damage anneals quietly away so the sheet is never done breaking; laminated glass, dicing tempered crumble, radiographic negative, sumi ink or feathered frost.

energy.doc: crack weight, specular gain and backdrop contrast — max hits hard, thick bright fractures over a lit pane

scale.doc: magnification of the fracture field about the x/y anchor — max nearly triples the crack geometry

speed.doc: crack-tip velocity and how often a fresh impact nucleates (0.2 still visibly propagates)

density.doc: how many impact sites live at once (2-10) and how many radials each throws

anneal.doc: how fast old damage heals away — low leaves the pane accumulating wreckage, high keeps it nearly clear

hue.doc: tint of the glass and the scene dimly visible behind it

x.doc: horizontal anchor of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical anchor of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: cool laminated pane with specular crack lips / tempered glass dicing into crumb rather than spidering / radiographic negative with fractures glowing white / sumi ink on cream / feathered cyan frost crazing

seed.doc: deterministic seed for impact placement, radial count and tip wander
